Exit guide
1. Run the crisis in Studio

Question: With generator gen-1 out, can the rest of the grid still serve demand, and at what cost?

If supply falls short, the optimisation sheds load at the value-of-lost-load penalty (10,000 PGLib cost units/MWh) and reports the unserved energy. The penalty is a modelling parameter, not an estimate of economic damage.

evidence.brief:
Feasible with 200 MWh unserved (77.22 % of demand)

OK:
The LOPF optimisation found a feasible dispatch (solver termination optimal) for a single period (no timestamp).
Evidence (4)
Info:
Scenario “PGLib IEEE 14-bus — loss of the main unit gen-1 (deliberate load shedding)” applies generator gen-1 out of service (the whole horizon); load shedding allowed as a penalised last resort, storage dispatch enabled.
Evidence (3)
Attention:
Out of service in this run: generator gen-1 (NG), which dispatched up to 259 MW in the baseline.
Evidence (2)
Critical:
200 MWh of demand is not served (77.22 % of 259 MWh), peak shedding 200 MW, over 1 h. Shedding is located at 10 buses: bus-3 (94.2 MWh), bus-9 (29.5 MWh), bus-14 (14.9 MWh), bus-13 (13.5 MWh), bus-6 (11.2 MWh) and 5 more.
Evidence (10)
OK:
No in-service branch reaches its thermal limit (≥ 99.9 % of s_nom); the most loaded is line branch-4 at 8.83 %.
Evidence (2)
Attention:
1 of 1 in-service generators with available capacity run at their availability limit in at least one snapshot (gen-2). In every snapshot with load shedding, all in-service generators with available capacity are at their limit: no generation headroom remains.
Evidence (1)
Info:
Compared with the baseline: unserved energy 0 MWh → 200 MWh; maximum branch loading 60.66 % → 8.83 % (−51.83 pp); operating cost +2 M PGLib cost units (+97,455 %).
Evidence (6)
Info:
Dispatch shifts versus baseline (energy by carrier): NG −200 MWh (−77.22 %).
Evidence (2)
Info:
The LP objective is 2 M PGLib cost units (benchmark cost coefficients (not a currency)), of which 2 M PGLib cost units is the load-shedding penalty and 1.37 k PGLib cost units generation cost. LP economics: the scenario VOLL of 10,000 PGLib cost units/MWh is a penalty term in the same objective, so the optimiser sheds load only where no feasible redispatch is cheaper than that penalty. At 10 shedding buses the nodal price equals the VOLL penalty, i.e. shedding is the marginal option there in the model. This is model economics, not a statement about real operator practice.
Evidence (9)

Assumptions
Deltas are scenario minus baseline, computed from the stored gridstorm-result documents.
Both runs use the same network dataset; differences reflect the scenario specification only within the stated model assumptions of each run.
Results are model outputs (provenance: modeled); deltas are provenance: calculated. They are not observations or predictions of real grid behaviour.
DC linearised power flow (LOPF) — no reactive power, voltage magnitudes or losses
Kirchhoff's voltage law imposed on a cycle basis with series reactances (x_pu_eff); branch active-power flow limited to s_nom x s_max_pu
Perfect foresight: all snapshots of the horizon are optimised jointly in one LP
Costs are short-run marginal costs from the dataset; nodal prices are LP duals of the nodal balance constraints
Modeled results for scenario analysis — not a validated blackout predictor or operational forecast
All monetary coefficients and legacy *_eur fields use PGLib cost units; no currency conversion is performed.
Benchmark coefficients have no verified currency year or exchange-rate provenance; they are not EUR or inflation-adjusted USD.
Secant linearisation is exact for linear costs, approximate for quadratic costs; startup, shutdown and fixed c0 costs are omitted.
VOLL is a scenario penalty in PGLib cost units/MWh, not a monetary estimate of outage damage.
Dataset dispatch set-points (p_set) released so the LOPF optimises dispatch: 5 generators
Load shedding modelled as one dispatchable generator per load bus (11 buses), marginal cost = VOLL 10000 PGLib cost units/MWh, bounded by the bus demand at every snapshot; VOLL is a penalty parameter, not an economic estimate
Synchronous condensers (carrier SYNC) have zero active-power capacity in the dataset
Export comparison report

Server-built report (gridstorm-comparison/1.0) incl. reproducibility hashes — last step of the guided demo.

evidence.verdict:
With storage dispatched, unserved energy is unchanged at 190.2 MWh: this mitigation does not change the load-shedding outcome. The LP objective changes by −342.4 k illustrative cost units (−1.75 %). Branches at their limit: 33 → 30. Storage discharges 24.78 GWh in the mitigated run.

Only mitigation.storage_dispatch differs (false → true); events, horizon and load shedding are identical.
